recent_posts.title: External import maps, today! • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript import maps can be injected dynamically today using a classic blocking script that creates a `<script type="importmap">` element via DOM methods and inserts it after itself using `document.currentScript.after()`. This technique works back to Chrome 89, Safari 16.4+, and Firefox 108+, and is already used by JSPM v4. The post provides minimal code examples including URL rebasing for relative paths and error handling. While this workaround reduces the urgency for native external import map support (`<script type="importmap" src="...">`) it doesn't eliminate the need — HTML remains the only way to include import maps, creating architectural debt and limitations like import maps not working in worker scripts. The author advocates for deeper platform-wide integration of specifiers and import maps, and hints at an upcoming tool for build-free dependency management built on top of JSPM Generator.

recent_posts.title: Web dependency management is broken and needs platform level solutions
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript dependency management on the web is fundamentally broken compared to other ecosystems. While Node.js and other platforms treat dependencies as first-class citizens, web developers must choose between fragile workarounds: deploying node_modules directly (security risk), using CDNs (reliability issues), or adopting bundlers for basic needs. Import maps exist but require HTML templating, manual mapping of every transitive dependency, and still need URLs to resolve to. The ecosystem has normalized this complexity, but it harms both newcomers and the platform's architecture. Proposed solutions include external import maps, HTTP header-based resolution, treating specifiers as a URL type, and server-side dependency resolution to make web dependencies truly first-class without requiring bundlers.

recent_posts.title: In the economy of user effort, be a bargain, not a scam • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: User effort should be treated as a currency that users spend to accomplish their goals. The key to great product design is creating a smooth complexity-to-effort curve where simple tasks remain easy while complex tasks are possible, avoiding usability cliffs where slight increases in complexity cause dramatic jumps in required effort. Products should maximize signal-to-noise ratio by eliminating unnecessary steps and boilerplate, prioritize consumer needs over producer needs, and design tradeoffs that make users feel they're getting a bargain rather than being overcharged for basic functionality.

recent_posts.title: State of HTML 2025 now open! • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: The State of HTML 2025 survey is now open for developers to participate. Led by Lea Verou, this annual survey directly influences browser vendor roadmaps and the Interop project prioritization. The survey includes 35 new features, removes 18 outdated ones, and introduces browser support icons for better clarity. Responses within the first two weeks will have higher impact on Interop 2026. The survey covers HTML-related JavaScript APIs, Web Components, and PWA features, with all questions being optional and available in multiple languages.

recent_posts.title: Influence the State of HTML 2025 Survey! • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: Lea Verou announces her return to lead the State of HTML 2025 survey, seeking community input on upcoming web platform features to include. The survey aims to influence browser vendor priorities and initiatives like Interop 2025, focusing on features mature enough to have specifications but not yet universally implemented. The 2023 survey achieved record participation with 21,000 developers and directly influenced Interop 2024 priorities including Popover API and Declarative Shadow DOM.

recent_posts.title: The Hovercar Framework for Deliberate Product Design • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: The Hovercar Framework proposes starting product design with an idealized North Star UI vision before working backwards to practical MVPs. This approach breaks complex product problems into three components: the ideal solution (North Star), current constraints, and reasonable compromises. The framework includes six stages from skateboard (bare minimum) to hovercar (unconstrained ideal), helping teams align on vision, make better tradeoffs, and create products that can evolve toward their ultimate goals. Case studies demonstrate how explicit North Star planning can make seemingly impossible features feasible through engineering momentum and iterative evolution.

recent_posts.title: Bluesky Likes Web Components • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: Lea Verou shares her experience building two web components for displaying Bluesky likes and likers, highlighting the challenges of creating accessible and localizable components. She praises the openness of Bluesky's API compared to other social platforms, discusses API design principles for web components, and details the complexities involved in proper accessibility implementation and internationalization. The article demonstrates how seemingly simple components can become complex when considering proper keyboard navigation, screen reader support, and multi-language functionality.

recent_posts.title: Construction Lines • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: Lea Verou reflects on her career transition after leaving Font Awesome, sharing insights about what drives professional happiness: autonomy, breadth, and impact. She discusses the value of diverse skillsets across web standards, product design, and developer relations, arguing against narrow specialization. Verou announces her return to consulting and entrepreneurship while making her open source work financially sustainable through sponsorship platforms.

recent_posts.title: Style-observer: observe CSS property changes, for reals • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: Style-observer is a new tool designed to detect CSS property changes and execute JavaScript in response, addressing limitations of previous methods. It performs feature detection to work around browser-specific bugs, supports throttling and aggregation, and has been exhaustively tested. The tool aims to provide a reliable solution for higher-level custom properties, polyfilling missing CSS features, and changing HTML attributes via CSS. Contributions for benchmarking are welcome.

recent_posts.title: Product • Lea Verou
recent_posts.summary: The author shares their early fascination with creating useful products and their journey from a young entrepreneur making handmade items to becoming a software engineer. They describe their passion for utility in product development, their experience in co-founding a startup, and the challenges they faced in academia. The narrative highlights their continuous drive to build products with real-world impact and the ultimate realization that product development, rather than traditional software engineering or academic research, is their true calling.

top_posts.title: Engineering Momentum as a Prioritization Factor • Lea Verou
top_posts.summary: Prioritization in software development balances various factors such as value, effort, and confidence. The RICE framework is popular for formalizing this process, considering Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort. An often overlooked factor is Engineering Interest, which can significantly influence project timelines. Including engineering interest in prioritization can boost morale and efficiency, as engineers are more motivated to work on tasks they are excited about. Adjusting frameworks like RICE to account for this can improve overall project outcomes.
